Effects of Estrogen: The corpus luteum produces a moderate amount of estrogen. It supports the lining of the endometrium.
Effects of Progesterone: The corpus luteum produces progesterone, which becomes the dominant hormone. Progesterone helps the endometrium to become receptive to implantation. It also produces a negative feedback on the brain, decreasing the production of the Luteinizing hormone (LH) and the Follicular stimulating hormone (FSH).
Effects of FSH: The level of the Follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) decreases because of the negative feedback caused by progesterone. This prevents further development of ovarian follicles.
Effects of LH: As progesterone becomes the dominant hormone, it triggers a negative feedback that reduces the production of the Luteinizing hormone (LH).
Energy Levels Info: You may still experience high energy from ovulation, still making it easier for high intensity activities. Muscles may work longer without getting tired, and the body will burn fat and not glucose. The best exercises to do are low intensity workouts such as cycling and running.
What to eat: During this phase it is best to eat carbs and proteins, as when doing exercise it will make your body rely on glucose less. Foods rich with vitamin B and healthy facts will also help to support hormonal balance, and therefore are recommended.
Foods and Recipes: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here.https://elara.care/nutrition/menstrual-cycle-food-chart/#mid-luteal-phase-foods
Concentration: Through the luteal phase, the dynamic complexity of the brain remains high but the activity patterns change. This supports deeper thinking, reflection and social sensitivity. For this time it is best to focus on work that requires close attention to detail, deep thinking, and planning.
Health: The luteal phase normally does not vary in length. If your luteal phase is 10 days or less it is recommended you go talk to a specialist as there is a possibility that you may experience Luteal phase deficiency (LPD). Some possible symptoms include spotting, short cycle, and >10 day luteal phase. This disease may contribute to infertility and lead to miscarriages.
Mood: The change in the hormones will result in mood swings, irritation and symptoms of PMS. During this time you might feel sad, angry and easily irritated. You might also feel more overwhelmed and less sociable.
Types of Vitamins: During the luteal phase the best vitamins and supplements to take consist of Vitamin B6, magnesium and zinc. Vitamin B6 will help reduce premenstrual symptoms and support hormonal balance. As well as zinc contributing to help support hormonal balance. The magnesium will help to reduce bloating and regulate mood swings.
Insights in the Brain: Progesterone becomes the dominant hormone, it produces a negative feedback on brain, decreasing the production of the Luteinizing hormone (LH) and the Follicular stimulating hormone (FSH).
Insights in the Ovaries: The ruptured follicles transition into the corpus luteum which produces a high amount of progesterone.
Insights in the Uterus: The uterus is prepared for a possible implantation.
Phase Info: The corpus luteum produces progesterones, it decreases the production of the Luteinizing hormone (LH) and the Follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) and prepares the uterus to welcome the implantation.
Today's Recap: Today you will still feel the energy from the ovulation and feel reflective. You might start experiencing mood swings throughout the week as you approach the late luteal phase.
